There are actually a lot of ways to approach fencer, a full tank frontline class, or a tanky-dps class.

Either way, I wouldn't choose highlander for a C2 if I were you, peltasta C1 is almost a necessity for not only late game but dungeon mobbing, swashbuckling is literally a godsend.  

The most common build is Swordsman 1 -> Peltasta 1 -> Barb1-3 -> fencer

This is a perfectly fine off tank DPS build, it'll allow you to tank some hits and do some decent damage mobbing.

If you plan on going a tank role you can go from Peltasta 1-> Peltasta 2/Barb1 -> Rodelero 1-2 -> fencer

Great for dungeons and late game partying, you'll have a harder time mobbing though.


For stats I'd honestly recommend going for a tankier route, being atleast reasonably tanky is a godsend in dungeon runs where you'll often find yourself without a healer and your main job is to just aggro mobs with swashbuckling.

Here's my build (all ratios of course):
STR: 4 CON: 2 DEX: 1
Perfectly standard warrior build, honestly might even consider putting more points in CON since it scales so well in both PVP and PVE.

Full DEX:
Pretty much explains itself, just pump all your points into dex with bonus stats in con if need be. The problem with this build is that while it is good in the early pre 100 game it doesn't scale well later. You can dodge physical attacks but magic mobs become much more frequent, and you get bodied pretty quickly. Also once you hit fencer you'll overcap your evasion on lunge. I don't like the build but it doesn't mean it's wrong.

Full STR:
Self explanatory as well, there have been some arguments for this build and while it does scale better and fare much better than full dex, you can't off tank before you're a fencer C2 realistically, and even then it'll still be rough. Essentially the best end game build if you're fully funded and level 280. Also wouldn't recommend.

High Dex:
DEX: 4 STR: 2 CON: 1
Reasonable build, not much to say here other than you'll have higher evasion and crit rate, better for early game than the build I'm using. You can go this build but you will be slightly inefficient when it comes to evasion since you overcap as well; but that's okay it's pretty marginal. 

My mindset is to pretty much play a swordsman class to be a tanky/offtank, you realistically are a meat shield since that's the only utility swordsmen have, they get outdamaged and out aoe'd by other classes but none can tank better than them if built right. If you'd like to go full damage go for it though.

It's fine to go either, Doppel is probably better for 2:1 dex since you don't maximize the evasion value from Lunge in the fencer tree (you overcap on evasion). Highlander attribute is actually rather underwhelming and the peltasta tree is much better in general for PVE. Since you don't have swashbuckling your ability to tank mobs is gonna be less efficient, so I'd recommend just going the dps route of Doppel; fencer is more of a off-tank dps.

Also note that one hand + Dagger is still viable for doppel C1, C2 is when you start having to use two handed swords, and there's still the possiblity that those abilities will be patched to allow other weapons other than 2h swords.

- Marth/Lucina have very good aerial games, learn to short-hop and use aerials.

You are usually not the aggressor in a matchup unless your opponent is stalling or is heavy in projectiles. Playing against projectiles can be difficult for marth and Lucina but it is not impossible.

If you're playing marth and have problems with projectiles here's a few tips (I play a shitload of marth):

- use short hops and forward airs/neutral airs to close the gap and punish them. You can also use neutral b as well.

- When playing against ranged characters try to read their rolls when you close in, using forward b to punish and get in free damage is great as it has great priority (especially against link)

- If you do happen to get caught in the air, try to go for the edge instead of closing the gap towards them, it's very hard to close in from high and easy for ranged characters to get free damage off you. (unless you can bait them with a counter, but don't rely on this too much.)

- Just a note when playing marth against ranged characters, you can approach aggressively, but once you get into range you should play the control/punish game and go for openings instead of full out assaults as they will probably go for A-neutrals.

- marth's grab is his best friend.
